nameShape.prompt: What is the name of this shape?
hints: Count the sides and the corners.
Check whether it has straight sides or is round.

nameSolid.prompt: What is the name of this solid shape?
hints: Is it round from every side?
Count the flat faces.

countOf.prompt: How many {shape} are there in the picture?
hints: Mark each one as you count it.
Be careful not to count the same shape twice.

countVertices.prompt: How many vertices (corners) does this shape have?
hints: A vertex is a point where two sides meet.
Count the pointed corners one by one.

countSides.prompt: How many sides does this shape have?
hints: A side is a straight edge of the shape.
Go around the shape and count the sides.

rulerRead.prompt: Use the ruler to find the length of the line. (cm)
hints: Find where the line starts and where it ends.
Subtract the starting mark from the ending mark.
rulerRead.expl: The line goes from {from} to {to}, so its length is {ans} cm.

lengthDiff.prompt: How many cm longer is the upper line than the lower line? (cm)
hints: Read both lengths first.
Subtract the shorter length from the longer one.

rightAngles.prompt: How many right angles does this shape have?
hints: A right angle looks like the corner of a square.
Check each corner one at a time.

clockMinutes.prompt: The clock shows {h} o'clock and some minutes. How many minutes? (min)
hints: Multiply the number the long hand points to by 5.
If the long hand points to 6 it is 30 minutes.
clockMinutes.expl: The long hand points to {n}, so ${n}\times5={ans}$ minutes.

mToCm.prompt: How many cm is {m} m {c} cm? (cm)
hints: 1 m is 100 cm.
Change the m to cm, then add the remaining cm.

triType.prompt: What kind of triangle has the side lengths shown?
hints: Compare the three side lengths.
Two equal sides: isosceles. Three equal sides: equilateral.

congruentCond.prompt: The two triangles are congruent. Which congruence condition applies?
hints: Find which sides are equal and which angles are equal.
Only sides: SSS. Two sides and the included angle: SAS. One side and the two angles at its ends: ASA.
congruentCond.expl: The equal parts in the picture are: {cond}. So this is the condition used.

circleDiameter.prompt: The radius of a circle is {r} cm. What is the diameter? (cm)
hints: The diameter is the longest segment through the centre.
The diameter is twice the radius.

circleRadius.prompt: The diameter of a circle is {d} cm. What is the radius? (cm)
hints: The radius goes from the centre to the circle.
The radius is half of the diameter.
A right angle is $90^\circ$.
Smaller than $90^\circ$ is acute; larger is obtuse.

angleThird.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are ${a}^\circ$ and ${b}^\circ$. What is the third angle? (degrees)
hints: The three angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
Subtract the two known angles from $180$.

angleQuad.prompt: Three angles of a quadrilateral are ${a}^\circ$, ${b}^\circ$ and ${c}^\circ$. What is the fourth angle? (degrees)
hints: The four angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.
Subtract the three known angles from $360$.

quadName.prompt: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
hints: Check whether opposite sides are parallel.
Also check whether all sides and angles are equal.

diagonals.prompt: How many diagonals does this shape have?
hints: A diagonal joins two vertices that are not next to each other.
First count the diagonals from one vertex.

perimeterRect.prompt: What is the perimeter of the rectangle? (cm)
hints: The perimeter is the distance around the shape.
Add the width and the height, then double it.

areaRect.prompt: What is the area of the rectangle? (cm²)
hints: The area of a rectangle is width × height.
Multiply the two lengths shown.

areaSquare.prompt: A square has sides of {s} cm. What is its area? (cm²)
hints: All four sides of a square are equal.
Multiply the side length by itself.

areaTriangle.prompt: A triangle has base {b} cm and height {h} cm. What is its area? (cm²)
hints: The area of a triangle is base × height ÷ 2.
The height is measured at a right angle to the base.

areaParallelogram.prompt: A parallelogram has base {b} cm and height {h} cm. What is its area? (cm²)
hints: The area of a parallelogram is base × height.
Use the height, not the slanted side.

areaTrapezoid.prompt: A trapezoid has top {a} cm, bottom {b} cm and height {h} cm. What is its area? (cm²)
hints: The area of a trapezoid is (top + bottom) × height ÷ 2.
First add the top and the bottom.

areaRhombus.prompt: The diagonals of a rhombus are {d1} cm and {d2} cm. What is its area? (cm²)
hints: The area of a rhombus is one diagonal × the other diagonal ÷ 2.
Multiply the diagonals, then divide by 2.

symmetryLines.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does this shape have?
hints: A line of symmetry folds the shape into two matching halves.
Try folding horizontally, vertically and diagonally.

congruentSide.prompt: The two triangles are congruent. What is the length of side $x$? (cm)
hints: Congruent shapes have the same shape and size.
Corresponding sides have equal lengths.

solidCount.prompt: How many {item} does a cuboid have?
hints: Picture a box.
Look at the top, bottom, front, back and both sides.

cuboidVolume.prompt: A cuboid is {l} cm long, {w} cm wide and {h} cm high. What is its volume? (cm³)
hints: The volume of a cuboid is length × width × height.
Multiply the three lengths.

cubeVolume.prompt: A cube has edges of {e} cm. What is its volume? (cm³)
hints: All edges of a cube are equal.
Multiply the edge length by itself three times.

cuboidSurface.prompt: A cuboid is {l} cm long, {w} cm wide and {h} cm high. What is its surface area? (cm²)
hints: The surface area is the sum of the six faces.
Opposite faces are equal: (lw + wh + lh) × 2.
cuboidSurface.expl: $({l}\times{w}+{w}\times{h}+{l}\times{h})\times2={ans}$, so the surface area is {ans} cm².

edgeSum.prompt: A cuboid is {l} cm long, {w} cm wide and {h} cm high. What is the total length of all its edges? (cm)
hints: A cuboid has 12 edges.
There are 4 edges each of length, width and height.

circumference.prompt: A circle has radius {r} cm. What is its circumference? (use $\pi=3.14$) (cm)
hints: Circumference = diameter × π.
The diameter is twice the radius.

circleArea.prompt: A circle has radius {r} cm. What is its area? (use $\pi=3.14$) (cm²)
hints: Area = radius × radius × π.
Multiply the radius by itself, then by 3.14.

prismFaces.prompt: How many faces does a prism with a {n}-sided base have?
hints: A prism has 2 bases and some side faces.
The number of side faces equals the number of sides of the base.
prismFaces.expl: {n} side faces plus 2 bases is {ans} faces.

adjacentAngle.prompt: On a straight line one angle is ${a}^\circ$. What is the adjacent angle? (degrees)
hints: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$.
Subtract the known angle from $180$.

verticalAngle.prompt: Two lines cross and one angle is ${a}^\circ$. What is the vertically opposite angle? (degrees)
hints: Vertically opposite angles face each other.
They are equal in size.
verticalAngle.expl: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is ${ans}^\circ$.

parallelAngle.prompt: Two parallel lines $l$ and $m$ are cut by a transversal. One angle is ${a}^\circ$. What is $x$? (degrees)
hints: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
Alternate angles are equal as well.
parallelAngle.expl: Corresponding (alternate) angles on parallel lines are equal, so $x={ans}$.

polygonSum.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with {n} sides? (degrees)
hints: A polygon with {n} sides splits into {m} triangles.
Each triangle has angle sum $180^\circ$.

regularAngle.prompt: What is one interior angle of a regular polygon with {n} sides? (degrees)
hints: First find the sum: $180\times({n}-2)$.
Divide the sum by the number of sides {n}.

arcLength.prompt: A sector has radius {r} cm and central angle ${a}^\circ$. Its arc length is $k\pi$ cm. What is $k$?
hints: Arc length is $2\pi r\times\frac{a}{360}$.
First find what fraction of the whole circle the angle is.

sectorArea.prompt: A sector has radius {r} cm and central angle ${a}^\circ$. Its area is $k\pi$ cm². What is $k$?
hints: Sector area is $\pi r^2\times\frac{a}{360}$.
Multiply the circle's area by the fraction of the angle.

cylinderVolume.prompt: A cylinder has base radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. Its volume is $k\pi$ cm³. What is $k$?
hints: Volume = base area × height.
The base area is $\pi r^2$.

coneVolume.prompt: A cone has base radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. Its volume is $k\pi$ cm³. What is $k$?
hints: Volume = base area × height ÷ 3.
The base area is $\pi r^2$.

sphereVolume.prompt: A sphere has radius {r} cm. Its volume is $k\pi$ cm³. What is $k$?
hints: The volume of a sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.
Cube the radius, then multiply by $\frac{4}{3}$.

sphereSurface.prompt: A sphere has radius {r} cm. Its surface area is $k\pi$ cm². What is $k$?
hints: The surface area of a sphere is $4\pi r^2$.
Square the radius, then multiply by 4.

cylinderSurface.prompt: A cylinder has base radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. Its surface area is $k\pi$ cm². What is $k$?
hints: Surface area = 2 × base area + lateral area.
The lateral area is (circumference) × height $=2\pi r\times h$.

isoscelesApex.prompt: A base angle of an isosceles triangle is ${b}^\circ$. What is the apex angle? (degrees)
hints: The two base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
Subtract both base angles from $180^\circ$.

parallelogramAngle.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, $\angle A={a}^\circ$. What is $\angle B$? (degrees)
hints: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to $180^\circ$.
Subtract $\angle A$ from $180$.

midSegment.prompt: In a triangle, segment $x$ joins the midpoints of two sides and is parallel to the third side, which is {s} cm. What is $x$? (cm)
hints: The segment joining two midpoints is half of the third side.
Divide {s} by 2.

similarSide.prompt: The two triangles are similar. What is the length of side $x$? (cm)
hints: In similar figures the ratios of corresponding sides are equal.
Find the scale factor first.

similarArea.prompt: Two similar figures have scale factor ${p}:{q}$. The smaller has area {s} cm². What is the area of the larger one? (cm²)
hints: The ratio of areas is the square of the scale factor.
Multiply the smaller area by $({q}/{p})^2$.

pythagHyp.prompt: The two shorter sides of a right triangle are {a} cm and {b} cm. What is the longest side $x$? (cm)
hints: Pythagorean theorem: $a^2+b^2=c^2$.
Square both sides, add them, then take the square root.

pythagLeg.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse {c} cm and one leg {a} cm. What is the other leg $x$? (cm)
hints: Take the square root of $c^2-a^2$.

pythagCheck.prompt: A triangle has sides {a} cm, {b} cm and {c} cm. Is it a right triangle?
hints: Take the longest side as the hypotenuse and compare $a^2+b^2$ with $c^2$.
If they are equal, it is a right triangle.

trigRatio.prompt: In the right triangle, what is $\{fn} A$? (write a decimal)
hints: $\sin A$ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, $\cos A$ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, $\tan A$ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
Tell the opposite and adjacent sides apart from angle $A$.
Recall the values for $30^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$.
$\sin30^\circ=\frac12$, $\cos60^\circ=\frac12$, $\tan45^\circ=1$.

trigSide.prompt: In a right triangle $\tan A={t}$ and the adjacent side is {adj}. What is the opposite side $x$?
hints: $\tan A$ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
Opposite $=\tan A\times$ adjacent.

inscribedAngle.prompt: The central angle on arc AB is ${c}^\circ$. What is the inscribed angle on the same arc? (degrees)
hints: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc.
Divide the central angle by 2.

tangentLength.prompt: From a point P outside circle O a tangent touches the circle at A. $PO={po}$ and the radius is {r}. What is $PA$?
hints: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so triangle OAP is right-angled.
Use $PA^2=PO^2-r^2$.

chordHalf.prompt: A circle has radius {r}. A chord is at distance {d} from the centre. What is the length of the chord?
hints: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.
Half the chord is $\sqrt{r^2-d^2}$.
chordHalf.expl: Half the chord is $\sqrt{{r}^2-{d}^2}={half}$, so the chord is ${ans}$.

cyclicAngle.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle and one angle is ${a}^\circ$. What is the opposite angle? (degrees)
hints: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to $180^\circ$.
Subtract the given angle from $180$.

distance.prompt: What is the distance between the points A({x1}, {y1}) and B({x2}, {y2}) on the coordinate plane?
hints: The distance is $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$.
Square the horizontal and vertical differences and add them.

midpoint.prompt: What is the ${axis}$-coordinate of the midpoint of segment AB with A({x1}, {y1}) and B({x2}, {y2})?
hints: The midpoint is the average of the coordinates.
Add the matching coordinates and divide by 2.

slope.prompt: What is the slope of the line through A({x1}, {y1}) and B({x2}, {y2})?
hints: Slope = (change in $y$) ÷ (change in $x$).
Compute $\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.

circleEqRadius.prompt: What is the radius of the circle $(x-{a})^2+(y-{b})^2={r2}$?
hints: In $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$ the right-hand side is $r^2$.
Take the square root of {r2}.

circleEqCenter.prompt: The circle $(x-{a})^2+(y-{b})^2={r2}$ has centre $(p, q)$. What is $p+q$?
hints: The centre is $(p, q)$.
Read $p$ and $q$ from $x-p$ and $y-q$.

pointLineDist.prompt: What is the distance from the origin to the line ${A}x+{B}y-{C}=0$?
hints: The distance from a point to a line is $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$.
For the origin $x_0=y_0=0$.

lawSinesR.prompt: In triangle ABC, $a={a}$ and $\angle A={A}^\circ$. What is the circumradius $R$?
hints: Law of sines: $\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R$.
Use the value of $\sin {A}^\circ$ to find $R$.

lawCosines.prompt: In triangle ABC, $a={a}$, $b={b}$ and $\angle C={C}^\circ$. What is $c$?
hints: Law of cosines: $c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$.
Substitute the value of $\cos {C}^\circ$.

areaSin.prompt: In triangle ABC, $a={a}$, $b={b}$ and $\angle C={C}^\circ$. What is its area?
hints: Area $=\frac12ab\sin C$.
Substitute the value of $\sin {C}^\circ$.
$180^\circ=\pi$ radians.
Simplify $\frac{{a}}{180}\pi$.

arcRad.prompt: A sector has radius {r} and central angle $\frac{\pi}{{d}}$. Its arc length is $k\pi$. What is $k$?
hints: Arc length is $l=r\theta$.
Multiply $r$ by $\theta=\frac{\pi}{{d}}$.

sectorRad.prompt: A sector has radius {r} and central angle $\frac{\pi}{{d}}$. Its area is $k\pi$. What is $k$?
hints: Sector area is $S=\frac12r^2\theta$.
Multiply $r^2$ by $\theta$, then by $\frac12$.

parabolaFocus.prompt: What is the $x$-coordinate of the focus of the parabola $y^2={k}x$?
hints: The focus of $y^2=4px$ is $(p, 0)$.
Solve $4p={k}$ for $p$.

ellipseFocal.prompt: The ellipse $\frac{x^2}{{a2}}+\frac{y^2}{{b2}}=1$ has foci $(\pm c, 0)$. What is $c$?
hints: For an ellipse $c^2=a^2-b^2$.
Subtract {b2} from {a2} and take the square root.

hyperbolaFocal.prompt: The hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{{a2}}-\frac{y^2}{{b2}}=1$ has foci $(\pm c, 0)$. What is $c$?
hints: For a hyperbola $c^2=a^2+b^2$.
Add {a2} and {b2} and take the square root.

vectorMag.prompt: What is the magnitude $|\vec{a}|$ of the vector $\vec{a}=({x}, {y})$?
hints: Square each component, add, and take the square root.

dotProduct.prompt: What is the dot product $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$ of $\vec{a}=({x1}, {y1})$ and $\vec{b}=({x2}, {y2})$?
hints: The dot product is $x_1x_2+y_1y_2$.
Multiply matching components and add.

vectorPerp.prompt: The vectors $\vec{a}=({x1}, k)$ and $\vec{b}=({x2}, {y2})$ are perpendicular. What is $k$?
hints: Perpendicular vectors have dot product $0$.
Solve $x_1x_2+ky_2=0$.

word.sss: Three pairs of sides are equal (SSS)
word.sas: Two sides and the angle between them are equal (SAS)
word.asa: One side and the two angles at its ends are equal (ASA)
word.yes: Yes, it is a right triangle
word.no: No, it is not a right triangle

E11.title: Shape names and corners
E11.concept: A **triangle** has 3 sides and a **quadrilateral** has 4 sides. A **circle** is round and has no corners.

E12.title: Solid shapes
E12.concept: A box shape is a **cuboid**, a round pillar is a **cylinder**, and a ball is a **sphere**.

E21.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals
E21.concept: A **triangle** has 3 straight sides and 3 corners; a **quadrilateral** has 4 straight sides and 4 corners, whatever its shape. Their number of sides equals their number of corners.

E22.title: Length and time
E22.concept: Put one end at 0 on the ruler; the mark at the other end is the length. $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. Multiply the number the long hand points to by 5 to get the minutes.

E31.title: Angles and right angles
E31.concept: Two rays from one point form an **angle**. A $90^\circ$ angle is a **right angle**; smaller is **acute**, larger is **obtuse**.

E32.title: Radius and diameter
E32.concept: The **radius** goes from the centre to the circle; the **diameter** passes through the centre. The diameter is twice the radius.

E41.title: Angle sums
E41.concept: The three angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$ and the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.

E42.title: Quadrilaterals and polygons
E42.concept: One pair of parallel sides makes a **trapezoid**, two pairs a **parallelogram**, and four equal sides a **rhombus**. A **diagonal** joins two vertices that are not neighbours.

E51.title: Perimeter and area
E51.concept: Rectangle: width × height. Triangle: base × height ÷ 2. Parallelogram: base × height. Trapezoid: (top + bottom) × height ÷ 2. Rhombus: diagonal × diagonal ÷ 2.

E52.title: Congruence and symmetry
E52.concept: Two shapes that match exactly are **congruent**. A shape that folds onto itself along a line is **symmetric**; that line is the **line of symmetry**.
E52.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry

E61.title: Circumference and circle area
E61.concept: Circumference = diameter × π, area = radius × radius × π, with π ≈ $3.14$.

E62.title: Cuboids and cubes
E62.concept: Volume = length × width × height; surface area = (sum of three face areas) × 2. A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

M11.title: Angle rules and polygons
M11.concept: Vertically opposite angles are equal; corresponding and alternate angles on parallel lines are equal. The interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon add up to $180^\circ\times(n-2)$.

M12.title: Sectors and solids
M12.concept: Arc length $=2\pi r\times\frac{a}{360}$, sector area $=\pi r^2\times\frac{a}{360}$, sphere volume $=\frac43\pi r^3$, cone volume $=\frac13\pi r^2h$.

M21.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals
M21.concept: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to $180^\circ$, and the segment joining two midpoints of a triangle is half the third side.

M22.title: Similarity and the Pythagorean theorem
M22.concept: Similar figures have equal side ratios and their areas are in the square of that ratio. In a right triangle $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

M31.title: Trigonometric ratios
M31.concept: In a right triangle $\sin A$ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, $\cos A$ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, $\tan A$ = opposite ÷ adjacent.

M32.title: Properties of circles
M32.concept: An inscribed angle is half the central angle on the same arc. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to $180^\circ$.

H11.title: Figures on the coordinate plane
H11.concept: Distance $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$, midpoint = average of coordinates, slope $\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.

H12.title: Equation of a circle
H12.concept: A circle with centre $(a, b)$ and radius $r$ is $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$. The distance from $(x_0,y_0)$ to $ax+by+c=0$ is $\frac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$.

H21.title: Triangles and trigonometric functions
H21.concept: Law of sines $\frac{a}{\sin A}=2R$, law of cosines $c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C$, triangle area $\frac12ab\sin C$.

H22.title: Radians and sectors
H22.concept: $180^\circ=\pi$ radians. A sector with radius $r$ and angle $\theta$ (radians) has arc length $r\theta$ and area $\frac12r^2\theta$.

H31.title: Conic sections
H31.concept: The parabola $y^2=4px$ has focus $(p,0)$; for the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $c^2=a^2-b^2$; for the hyperbola $c^2=a^2+b^2$.

H32.title: Plane vectors
H32.concept: The magnitude of $(x,y)$ is $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$; the dot product is $x_1x_2+y_1y_2$, and perpendicular vectors have dot product 0.
